title: Deployment quarantine ladders and proximity-aware fallback orchestration
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: We currently have several rollout primitives (canaries, A/B, shadowing) but lack a concise, testable topology for quarantining risky model variants before they reach production capacity tiers or cross-region traffic. This ticket proposes a quarantine-ladder routing component that: 1) ensures compatibility and small-surface exposure for new variants (prefix probes + deterministic subset routing), 2) applies proximity/latency-penalties when deciding fallback targets during capacity or region failure, and 3) integrates with quality-based auto-rollback triggers (metric windows and semantic regression signals).

Goals:
- Define quarantine lanes and their lifecycle (probe -> soft-canary -> ladder escalation -> release).
- Implement proximity-aware fallback rules so traffic prefers same-region low-latency fallbacks before cost-tier fallbacks.
- Add variant-compatibility gating so only compatible API schemas and KV-cache formats are routed into higher tiers.
- Wire quality and infra signals into an automated rollback engine with configurable hysteresis.

Deliverables:
- Router component design doc and state machine for quarantine ladders.
- API for declaring compatibility metadata on model variants (schema hash, kv-compat flag, kv-version).
- Fallback priority algorithm (region affinity score + capacity tier penalty + compatibility penalty).
- Integration tests and a canary run using the search-ranking reference workload.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strict compatibility gating reduces rollout velocity but avoids runtime incompatibility errors that cause expensive rollbacks.
- Proximity-first fallbacks may increase cost if cross-region cold pools are preferred; we will expose a penalty parameter to tune cost/latency balance.
- More complex state machine increases operational surface area; we'll start with a two-lane ladder (probe -> soft-canary) and iterate to n-ladders after initial telemetry shows value.
